name: Legal
blurb: Research, review, and drafting at scale, the citation-sanction lesson, and the benchmarks and trade bodies that measure legal AI accuracy.

points.desc: The ABA Center for Innovation's AI work, including Formal Opinion 512 on generative AI ethics, is the profession's reference point.
points.name: The ABA carries the profession's guidance

points.desc: The Legal Models section tracks models tuned for legal text, and the lawsuit tracker follows the AI docket itself.
points.name: Legal models are catalogued on this site

points.desc: Independent evaluation of models on legal research, case-law synthesis, and statutory interpretation - the vendor-neutral test of whether legal AI actually reasons.
points.name: Vals AI benchmarks legal reasoning

points.desc: A research database categorizing global legal technology and AI vendors - the map of what exists before evaluating what works.
points.name: Legaltech Hub catalogues the tools

points.desc: The International Legal Technology Association's annual technology survey is the record of actual purchasing and deployment across law firms.
points.name: ILTA surveys what firms buy

points.desc: The center for legal informatics tracks legal technology innovation, access-to-justice tools, and computational law research.
points.name: Stanford CodeX studies legal informatics

reading.body:
Legal AI has moved from experimentation to deployment, but the profession's defining lesson is that unverified citations invite sanctions, so verification is now the industry standard.

The six reference points span guidance, cataloguing, benchmarking, purchasing data, and academic research. The ABA sets ethics guidance, Legaltech Hub maps the tools, Vals AI benchmarks legal reasoning, ILTA records what firms actually buy, and Stanford CodeX studies the underlying informatics. Together they cover what exists, what works, and what gets deployed.

This matters for AI because legal work is high-stakes text reasoning where errors carry professional liability. Independent benchmarks and ethics opinions act as gatekeepers, not raw model capability. The data does not cover compute, power, or infrastructure costs, and it gives no adoption numbers or performance scores, so it cannot support claims about scaling constraints.

summary: Research, review, and drafting assistance are deployed at scale; sanctions for unverified citations made verification the industry lesson.
